# Charter — T13 tool platform (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

- **Project:** T13 'Tool platform', track v2, ADM phase G, plateau capability, tranche 3, project `01a1d039-0d37-730f-8f8a-2f50e5a0933d`, plan `docs/SPEC_V2.md#12` (the T13 row in SPEC_V2 §12). The row records `meta.measured_status: built`, `meta.depends_on: [T2 (needs), P0 (needs)]`, `meta.issues: [76, 556, 557, 630]` — all four closed on GitHub — and `meta.expected_outputs: [project-brief, evidence]`. It was reopened for the #526 retrospective rework under delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14` with the reason 'the retrospective MSP/TOGAF/SAFe rework of tranche 3 (#526)', and the rework runs against the acceptance receipt `docs/evidence/rework/T13.json`, which is red on the mandatory artefact packages and on the P1 package v1-p116-1.
- **Mandate:** give every conveyor-internal run exactly one governed way to reach a job backend — `tools.call` — with the binding row as its authority, refusal before dispatch, one `tool_call` ledger row per call, credential brokerage over sealed secrets, and tenant-prefixed object storage. The retrospective reconstitutes the MSP/TOGAF lifecycle record for that slice: charter, Statement of Architecture Work, the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable, the Phase-G review, the project-brief and evidence outputs and the closure review.
- **Scope:** in — the broker `tools.call` and its seven steps; the `tool`, `toolkit`, `tool_binding` and `tool_call` tables; effect classes read, write, destructive and spend; binding-scoped credential aliases; the direct MinIO storage adapter with the `tenant/<tenant_id>/` prefix; the coding toolkit and one kag-era toolkit; V1's external actions migrated; the six §12 gate proofs. Out — the catalogue actions and the estate import (T14); the agent platform gateway `nonagenticai_mcp_server` (D44, D59); the BYO publication surface (v1-w4a-6); live MinIO wiring (v1-p1110-1); a production `tool_binding` writer (v1-p111-1).
- **Date:** this charter is retrospective and was authored on 2026-11-26; it records the lifecycle of a build proved on 2026-11-22 at lane head 582e2dc6, it does not authorise new work, and it does not re-run the suite.

The architecture work is the tool platform itself — the broker, the call ledger, the effect and schema gates and the tenant-prefixed storage adapter — recorded retrospectively and dated 2026-11-26.
body.scope: In scope: the broker tools.call and its seven steps (resolve the binding, check effect and budget, validate the closed schema, resolve the credential alias, call the registered destination, normalise and redact, record and emit); the tool, toolkit, tool_binding and tool_call tables; effect classes read, write, destructive and spend with tenant-configured approvals, dry-run and dual control; credential aliases over sealed secrets; the direct MinIO adapter with tenant, project and run prefixes; the coding toolkit and one kag-era toolkit; V1's external-action migration; the six §12 gate proofs. Out of scope: catalogue actions and the estate import, which T14 owns; the agent platform gateway nonagenticai_mcp_server, permanently outside the conveyor's path (D44, D59); the BYO publication surface (v1-w4a-6); live MinIO wiring (v1-p1110-1); a production tool_binding writer (v1-p111-1).

Eight actors on the influence, interest and engagement axes. The development job family is the consumer whose only path to a backend is tools.call. The programme owner and the Architecture Board hold the decision and the approval, and the board acts under the standing delegation with an approver distinct from the requester. The programme architect is responsible for this retrospective record. The coding fleet owner registers the destination alias, tenant admins configure destructive approvals and BYO publication, and the platform operator publishes versions, probes and retires. The agent platform gateway is named as a boundary rather than a consumer.

## Links

## Document

Purpose: place the actors of the tool platform so each concern has a named owner and a stated engagement. Scope: the stakeholders of the tool platform and its two contracts. It was reconstructed retrospectively on 2026-11-26 from the recorded roles, not from a live elicitation, and it does not claim that any actor re-accepted the platform after the 2026-11-22 record.

# Driver/goal/objective — T13 tool platform

## Metadata

Retrospective catalog for T13, authored 2026-11-26 from SPEC_V2 §11.1–§11.10, the T13 row in SPEC_V2 §12 and the project transcript. Phase a, plateau psa, kind catalog; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation; reviewer the Architecture Board; project 01a1d039-0d37-730f-8f8a-2f50e5a0933d.

## Entries

Seven drivers, each with a goal and a measurable objective. D1 records the ad-hoc call and G1 makes one broker path. D2 records the second-control-plane pressure and G2 refuses it while borrowing the catalogue shape. D3 records secret leakage and G3 keeps keys out of prompts and ledgers. D4 records ungoverned destructive effects and G4 gates them on tenant approvals. D5 records backend-side rejection and G5 refuses invalid input before egress. D6 records caller-built keys and G6 lets the adapter build every tenant-prefixed key. D7 records invisible calls and G7 writes one ledger row and one event per call.

## Links

This artefact carries one typed edge: Stakeholder map — T13 tool platform as derivation, because the drivers are held by the actors named there. Every edge names another artefact this pack creates, so the set has no orphan.

## Document

Purpose: trace why the tool platform exists and what it is meant to achieve. Scope: the drivers and goals of one governed call path. It was authored retrospectively on 2026-11-26 from SPEC_V2 §11 and the proving suite, and it records the objective the slice set rather than claiming a wider capability than the six proofs support.

# Solution concept — T13 tool platform

## Metadata

Retrospective diagram for T13, authored 2026-11-26 from SPEC_V2 §11.1–§11.10, the T13 row in SPEC_V2 §12 and the project transcript. Phase a, plateau psa, kind diagram; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation; reviewer the Architecture Board; project 01a1d039-0d37-730f-8f8a-2f50e5a0933d.

## Entries

Thirteen rows: nine components and four edges. The broker is one seven-step path with refusal before egress. The four tables hold the operation, the immutable bundle, the tenant-scoped binding and the ledger. Credential profiles put sealed secrets behind aliases; the adapter owns every tenant-prefixed key; the alias registry keeps the destination out of the caller's hands; verify-then-judge makes a write carry its read-back. The four edges record the path from authority to evidence, with a refusal at each step rather than a silent repair.

## Links

This artefact carries one typed edge: Requirements catalog — T13 tool platform as realization, because the components exist to satisfy those requirements. Every edge names another artefact this pack creates, so the set has no orphan.

## Document

Purpose: show the components and edges that turn a bound call into one governed destination call and one ledger row. Scope: the broker, the tables, credentials, the alias registry, the adapter and the write verification. It was drawn retrospectively on 2026-11-26 from the build order in SPEC_V2 §11.3 and the tests, not from a design session held before the work.

# Business capability map — T13 tool platform

## Metadata

Retrospective diagram for T13, authored 2026-11-26 from SPEC_V2 §11.1–§11.10, the T13 row in SPEC_V2 §12 and the project transcript. Phase b, plateau hld, kind diagram; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation; reviewer the Architecture Board; project 01a1d039-0d37-730f-8f8a-2f50e5a0933d.

## Entries

Eight capabilities. Tool and toolkit lifecycle makes every callable operation an immutable version. Binding-scoped access gives a run exactly what its binding pins. Broker dispatch makes one path real. Effect-class gating separates read, write, destructive and spend, and its approved execution path is the one capability recorded as open. Input enforcement refuses a closed-schema violation before egress. The ledger makes each call visible. Storage separates tenant bytes under an adapter-built key. Probe and retirement is specified and enabled here, exercised by the estate import in T14.

## Links

Purpose: name the capabilities the tool platform establishes and the evidence each leaves behind. Scope: lifecycle, access, dispatch, gating, enforcement, ledger, storage and retirement. It is retrospective and dated 2026-11-26; it records the capability set as proved on 2026-11-22 and states plainly which capability the record leaves open rather than upgrading it.

value.usage: a new tool is a crate or service in the conveyor monorepo registered from its own OpenAPI; a migrated tool joins when rewritten in Rust (D58)

value.usage: the proving suite runs a fresh Postgres 18 and writes tenant-scoped through begin_scoped; the four tables live in the same schema as the reused rows

value.usage: the adapter talks to the shared MinIO instance directly, with no artifact_service or storage-api dependency, and the tenant prefix plus bucket policy carry the separation

value.usage: Draft 2020-12 with additionalProperties false, enums, patterns and bounds; a violation returns 422 tool_input_invalid with errors[] before egress

entries.axis_b: registered HTTP aliases

value.usage: the base URL is registered and reviewed at publication and resolved at call time, so no caller-supplied URL is admitted (the SSRF rule)

entries.axis_b: OpenAPI 3.1 and streamable-HTTP MCP

value.usage: exactly two forms; a remote MCP server is discovered binding-scoped and every BYO destination is tenant-allowlisted at registration

entries.axis_b: a counting HTTP stub

value.usage: every refusal asserts on the wire: a refused call that reached upstream would move the counter; the suite serialises because the destination URL is process-global

entries.axis_b: keys and bounded polls

value.usage: writes take an idempotency_key and replay the stored response; a poll has a fixed budget and a timeout returns pending with a resume_token

# Technology standards — T13 tool platform

## Metadata

Retrospective catalog for T13, authored 2026-11-26 from SPEC_V2 §11.1–§11.10, the T13 row in SPEC_V2 §12 and the project transcript. Phase d, plateau hld, kind catalog; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation; reviewer the Architecture Board; project 01a1d039-0d37-730f-8f8a-2f50e5a0933d.

## Entries

Eight standards. The workspace keeps tool code in one Rust repository. Postgres 18 holds the four tables and the reused rows under tenant-scoped writes. MinIO is reached directly by the adapter, with the tenant prefix as the separation rule. The closed schema subset decides input before egress. Destination aliases keep URLs out of a caller's hands, and the two BYO protocols are fixed at OpenAPI 3.1 and streamable-HTTP MCP. The counting stub makes each refusal a wire assertion, and idempotency keys with bounded polls keep retries safe.

## Links

This artefact carries one typed edge: Data entity catalog — T13 tool platform as derivation, because each entity is held in one of these formats. Every edge names another artefact this pack creates, so the set has no orphan.

## Document

Purpose: name the formats, protocols and instruments the tool platform relies on. Scope: the workspace, the database, the object store, the schema subset, addressing, BYO protocols, instrumentation and idempotency. It was authored retrospectively on 2026-11-26 and names only standards that SPEC_V2 §11 and the proving suite actually apply, with no version pin asserted beyond what the sources state.

Each carries its own entries: eight stakeholders, seven drivers, ten requirements, thirteen components and edges, eight capabilities, nine entities and eight standards, so the index points at authored content rather than at an empty shell.

Every edge names another artefact of this pack, so no artefact is an orphan.

## Document

The index is the architecture-artifact page the artefact standard reads, published in the rework batch as 01a20525-8994-7731-84a8-bb7e310e7ba0. It records the seven artefact rows approved on 2026-11-22 and re-published with their authored bodies in this retrospective pack dated 2026-11-26; it does not claim that the board re-reviewed any artefact after 2026-11-22, and it names no artefact the record does not carry.

risk.title: The approved destructive execution path is not proved — only its refusal is
risk.body: The T13 suite proves a_destructive_call_without_approvals_is_refused at the wire: 403 approval_required, zero destination hits and no ledger row. It does not prove an approved destructive call executing under the tenant's configured approvals, dry-run and dual control, so the positive half of SPEC_V2 §11.4 remains an open finding rather than a delivered capability. This retrospective row, recorded 2026-11-26, keeps the gap visible instead of reading the refusal as the whole gate.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

risk.title: The storage round trip falls back to the in-memory store, so live MinIO stays unproved
risk.body: a_job_round_trips_a_tenant_prefixed_object checks the tenant prefix, sha256 equality, read-back bytes, a wrong-hash refusal, head and a traversal refusal, but when no endpoint is configured the test uses the in-memory store. Live MinIO wiring is the recorded open item v1-p1110-1, so the bytes-separation claim is proved against the adapter's contract rather than against the deployed bucket. Recorded 2026-11-26.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

risk.title: The destination URL is process-global, so a parallel runner would produce false refusals
risk.body: The proving suite serialises on one lock because the destination URL is process-global. Under a parallel test runner two tests would swap the destination and the counting stub would report hits against the wrong case, so a refusal could pass or fail for the wrong reason. The record keeps the suite serialised; this retrospective row of 2026-11-26 states the trap so a later runner change is not made silently.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

issue.title: No production tool_binding writer exists — bindings are written directly in the suite
issue.body: The binding row is the broker's authority, but the slice ships no production writer for it: the test header says tool rows are written directly in the proving suite. The recorded open item v1-p111-1 carries this, and a real run therefore depends on the catalogue path that T14 and the tenant authoring surface own. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

requirements: docs/SPEC_V2.md#12 — the binding is the authority

issue.title: Catalogue actions and the estate import are deferred to T14
issue.body: This slice ships no catalogue actions and no estate import; it proves the broker against a coding toolkit and one kag-era toolkit and leaves the broad import, the published tool contract and the binding and catalogue actions to T14, which depends on T13. Issues #556 and #557 record that follow-on work, both closed. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

assumption.title: The six §12 proofs are sufficient evidence of the gate
assumption.body: The acceptance evidence is the named tests in crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs, 17 of 17 passed at lane head 582e2dc6 on 2026-11-22 against a fresh Postgres 18 and a counting HTTP stub. The assumption is that those tests, not a manual run, are the gate: each §12 clause maps to a named test and each refusal asserts on the wire. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

assumption.title: No destructive call is bound before its tenant configures approvals
assumption.body: With no configured approvals the broker refuses 403 approval_required and makes no destination call, so the default posture is refusal rather than dispatch. The assumption is that a tenant cannot bind a destructive tool into a run without first configuring the approvals the effect class requires. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

assumption.title: Directly written test rows exercise the same resolution the broker performs in production
assumption.body: Because the slice ships no catalogue write path, the suite writes tool, toolkit and tool_binding rows directly. The assumption is that the broker's resolution — binding, pinned toolkit version, effect ceiling and credential alias — reads the same rows a production writer would create, so the proof transfers despite the missing writer. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

dependency.title: T13 needs T2's run and queue, and T14 needs T13
dependency.body: The project record names depends_on as needs T2 and needs P0. T2 supplies the run and durable-queue context that tool_binding.run_id targets and that the broker's step and run ids reference; P0 supplies the constitution and gates. Downstream, T6, T7, T14, T15, T16 and T17 depend on T13, and T14's estate import is the first consumer. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

dependency.title: Calls depend on a reviewed destination alias, never a caller-supplied URL
dependency.body: Every call resolves a destination alias registered and reviewed at publication; the coding fleet owner supplies the alias and no caller-supplied URL is admitted at call time. The dependency is one way: a fleet moving its base URL requires a new reviewed alias before a run can reach it. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

benefit.title: A job reaches a backend only through one governed call path
benefit.body: The broker resolves the binding, checks effect and budget, validates the schema and resolves the credential before any network call, so an unbound, over-ceiling or invalid call is refused with zero destination hits. The benefit is that no procedure or agent can reach a backend by an ad hoc HTTP call, and the ledger row plus the tool.called event make every dispatched call attributable to a run and a step. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

benefit.title: Job bytes are tenant-separated without a compatibility shim
benefit.body: The adapter writes and reads MinIO directly under tenant/<tenant_id>/ with project and run prefixes, verifies a sha256 content hash, refuses a traversal name and applies a size cap, while the compiled prompt carries no S3 key. The benefit is that a job's objects are separated by the adapter's own key construction rather than by a legacy artifact service, and the round-trip test proves the contract. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

project_brief_output:
# Project brief — T13 tool platform (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Outcome

T13 made one governed call path real: every conveyor-internal run reaches a job backend through tools.call under a binding row's authority, with the effect class, the tool budget and the closed input schema decided before any network call, and exactly one tool_call row and one tool.called event recorded per dispatched call. The six SPEC_V2 §12 clauses are proved by named wire-level tests in crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs, 17 of 17 passed at lane head 582e2dc6 on 2026-11-22 against a fresh Postgres 18 and a counting HTTP stub.

## Boundary

Out of scope: the catalogue actions and the estate import, which T14 owns; the agent platform gateway nonagenticai_mcp_server, which serves the agent platform's own backends and stays outside the conveyor's path (D44, D59); the BYO publication surface (v1-w4a-6); live MinIO wiring (v1-p1110-1); and a production tool_binding writer (v1-p111-1). The slice must not fork T2's run or durable queue, must not become a second catalogue or runner, and must not carry a credential or an S3 key into a prompt or a ledger row.

## Reuse sources

- conveyor_store::secret::create_secret_tx — sealed credentials, reused rather than rebuilt (§11.8).
- governed_asset kind='tool_draft' — the publication lifecycle of validation, security review, tools.publish and binding (§11.6).
- event and audit_event — the tool.called event and the audit trail (§11.3 step 7).
- T2's run and durable queue — tool_binding.run_id targets a run, and §12 places T13 after T2.
- The predecessor MCP server's coding toolkit as a reference shape only: eleven operations and the mcp_tool_call_audit model, never routed through (D44, D59).

## Inception units

The analysis T13 starts from is SPEC_V2 §11.1–§11.10 and the T13 row in SPEC_V2 §12, and its recorded entry point is issue #76, with the follow-on issues #556 (bound toolkits reach the agent executor), #557 (binding and catalogue actions and the full published tool contract) and #630 (the run inspector's executor kind, binding pin and tools panel), all closed on GitHub. The retrospective reconstitutes the governance record over the completed slice — charter, Statement of Architecture Work, the seven A–D artefacts approved by the board, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable, the Phase-G review, the project brief, the evidence and the closure review.

## Dependencies

The project record names depends_on as needs T2 (the run and durable-queue context that tool_binding.run_id targets) and needs P0 (the constitution and gates). In the other direction, T6, T7, T14, T15, T16 and T17 depend on T13, with T14's estate import as the first consumer, and a job's calls additionally depend on a destination alias registered and reviewed at publication. In governance the slice depends on the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14 and on the approvals 01a20273-4f0f-77e6-8005-9744d1e3a574 and 01a20277-4be1-78c6-8516-728eb4d6068b.

## Acceptance

The SPEC_V2 §12 gate, executed through acceptance/programme/T13.toml and six named tests: a_bound_job_calls_coding_through_the_broker; one_call_is_one_ledger_row; a_destructive_call_without_approvals_is_refused; a_closed_schema_refuses_before_the_call; a_job_round_trips_a_tenant_prefixed_object; the_compiled_prompt_carries_no_s3_key. Each refusal is asserted on the wire through a counting HTTP stub, so a refusal that reached upstream would fail. The recorded run is 17 of 17 passed at lane head 582e2dc6 on 2026-11-22 against a fresh Postgres 18.

## Capabilities

The platform exercises an immutable tool and toolkit lifecycle; binding-scoped access that narrows but never widens; broker dispatch as the single path to a backend; effect-class gating for read, write, destructive and spend; closed-schema input enforcement before egress; a call ledger that makes each call and its cost visible; tenant-separated object storage under an adapter-built tenant prefix with a content hash; and the probe and retirement rules that T14's estate toolkits exercise.

## Plan

The plan is one WBS deliverable, 'The tool platform — one governed call path, the call ledger, the schema and effect gates, and tenant-prefixed storage', accepted with WSJF inputs 8, 5, 8 and 5 and evidenced by acceptance/programme/T13.toml and the proving suite. It sits in tranche 3, whose review records continue. This brief is retrospective and dated 2026-11-26: it records the slice proved on 2026-11-22 and the governance reconstituted over it, and it does not claim a fresh gate run or a capability the six proofs do not carry.

# Evidence — T13 tool platform (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Claim

T13 implements SPEC_V2 §11's broker, ledger, gates and storage adapter, and the six §12 clauses are proved by named wire-level tests: a bound development job calls coding through the broker; one call writes one tool_call row and one tool.called event; a destructive call without the tenant's approvals is refused; schema-invalid input is refused before the backend call; a job writes and reads a tenant-prefixed object with no S3 key in the prompt; and the compiled prompt carries no credential.

## Evidence

The proving suite is crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs: 17 tests, re-run for the record as 17 of 17 passed at lane head 582e2dc6 on 2026-11-22 against a fresh Postgres 18 and a counting HTTP stub. The manifest is acceptance/programme/T13.toml. The governance record is the Statement of Architecture Work 01a20271-2a37-7329-b159-28031ddcb966 under approval 01a20273-4f0f-77e6-8005-9744d1e3a574, the delivery contract 01a20277-2d08-7c91-bce6-1a8326add30c under approval 01a20277-4be1-78c6-8516-728eb4d6068b, and the scope baselines 01a20277-9131-7ee2-acad-7e40ffa8f947 and 01a20279-854d-79f6-a751-a34d51be7589. The seven A–D artefact rows 01a20275-1783-769e-9744-fa9246b22916, 01a20275-6094-70ad-89a6-512086e3a162, 01a20275-a8ee-7e43-afaa-505a452e314d, 01a20275-f69f-77aa-b414-595b4337e30c, 01a20276-3c76-793c-a765-68b0210bcb5e, 01a20276-82e4-7594-b73b-60590e969803 and 01a20276-c56b-75f2-b9bd-9ddaba1dd95f carry the authored bodies.

## Verification

Run the tool_platform suite through the build guard at the recorded sha: it needs a fresh Postgres 18 and starts a counting HTTP stub, so a refusal that called upstream moves the counter and fails. The suite serialises on one lock because the destination URL is process-global. Each of the six proofs asserts on the wire rather than on an error string, and the extra tests show a missing credential refusing 409 tool_not_ready, a call-time ceiling raise refused, the binding's sealed credential used and a keyed write replayed with one destination call. This content pack is checked offline by scripts/rework-content-check.py --project T13 before the factory reads it.

## Links

The plan section is SPEC_V2 §12 (the T13 row) over §11.1–§11.10. The governance record is the Statement of Architecture Work 01a20271-2a37-7329-b159-28031ddcb966, the delivery contract 01a20277-2d08-7c91-bce6-1a8326add30c approved by 01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545 rather than the requester 01a1e607-17d9-77d3-98d3-a43a87c4633d, the Phase-G reviews on the statement and on the delivery contract at level compliant, the tranche-3 review, and the published outputs: the project brief 01a20279-c813-754b-902b-f85be7ede1cd, the evidence 01a1f2cc-d575-7766-a4c6-a50af370f369 and the closure review. The transcript is docs/evidence/rework/T13/transcript.jsonl.

## Gap

Several limits are recorded and none is closed by this pack. The receipt lists the P1 package v1-p116-1 as unresolved. There is no production tool_binding writer (v1-p111-1), so the suite writes tool rows directly; the storage round trip uses the in-memory store when no endpoint is configured (v1-p1110-1), so live MinIO is unproved; the destructive path is proved only for its refusal, not for an approved execution; the kag-era toolkit and V1's external-action migration are recorded but not exercised by a live call; and the sub-features of v1-w4a-5, v1-p111-3, v1-p118-2 and v1-w4a-6 remain open. Two traps are carried: the destination URL is process-global, so the suite serialises, and a zero-call tool is only flagged, not yet retired, until T14 exercises the probe.

## Outcome vs acceptance

The outcome the charter records is one governed call path to a job backend, and the acceptance the record carries matches it: the six SPEC_V2 §12 clauses are proved by the named tests in crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs, 17 of 17 passed at lane head 582e2dc6 on 2026-11-22 against a fresh Postgres 18 and a counting HTTP stub, each refusal asserted on the wire with zero destination hits.
